atlas:
Use case: stylized-concept / style-transfer. Asset: tiny tabletop hotbar glyph candidates. Create ONE square atlas in NINE EQUAL cells, a strict 3x3 row-major grid, without drawn grid lines or cell labels. PURE SOLID WHITE #FFFFFF silhouettes on perfectly clean PURE BLACK #000000. Reference 1 supplies the approved WHITE-GLYPH STYLE ONLY; do not copy its subjects. Each icon must fit in the central 60 percent of its own cell, leaving at least 20 percent black margin on every side. No part may cross a cell boundary. All human heads, feet, hands and tool ends must remain complete. Broad sober stencil shapes, generous large negative spaces, minimal featureless faces and natural adult anatomy, readable at 64, 32 and 16 px. No gray, shading, gradients, texture, hatching, dithering, speckles, distressed edges, thin hair or fabric detail, labels, initials, numerals, border or watermark. No anime, heroic faces, chibi, giant generic cogs, playful arrows, gore or monsters. This is a PLAYER HUMAN action set: no harpies, birds, bees, wings or machine anatomy. The TWO requested variations must offer genuinely distinct readable concepts or poses, not three copies. No pictorial text anywhere.

Reference 1 supplies WHITE-GLYPH STYLE ONLY. Reference 2 is the SELECTED EXISTING FIGURE to develop. Keep its ordinary human design but zoom out, add an assailant at RIGHT, extend the retreating person's RIGHT HAND BEHIND, and show a torso-pivot ROTATION ARROW. The GM specifically requests this one functional arrow; it must be sober and minimal. Do not copy the older two-person barred-strike design.
GM feedback, verbatim: Zoom out to fit two people. Add an assailant to the right of the existing figure. Add a arrow indicating rotation of the retreating man. The retreating man is extending his right hand behind.
ROW-MAJOR CONTENTS:
1. Keep the reference's ordinary adult man as the LEFT figure, but zoom out enough to fit TWO COMPLETE adult figures within one icon. Add ONE assailant at the RIGHT, facing LEFT and reaching toward the withdrawing man. The LEFT man's torso turns to face LEFT, one foot stepping LEFT to withdraw, while his head turns BACK RIGHT to watch the assailant. His RIGHT ARM EXTENDS BEHIND HIM TO THE RIGHT, open palm outward toward the assailant, maintaining a guarded separation; his left arm remains near the front of his body. The assailant's reaching hand stops short of that rearward palm, no blow lands. Show ONE stout short CURVED ROTATION ARROW beside the withdrawing man's hips, indicating his torso pivot to the left, not travel and not an arrow between people. Two naturally proportioned full bodies, sober unarmed controlled withdrawal, not a sprint or blind flight. Both right-hand fingers and palm are grouped as a simple anatomically coherent hand. No added weapon, prohibition circle, crossed-fist badge, impact star, wings or third person.
2. Develop the reference into TWO COMPLETE ordinary adult humans, retreating man at LEFT and assailant at RIGHT. In a front-three-quarter view the LEFT man makes a controlled QUARTER-TURN TOWARD LEFT, body already angled to step away LEFT, HEAD still LOOKING BACK RIGHT at the assailant. His RIGHT ARM is clearly EXTENDED BEHIND HIS TORSO toward the RIGHT, with its OPEN PALM checking the outside of the assailant's reaching left WRIST. His left hand stays in a compact protective position in front of his chest. The RIGHT assailant leans slightly LEFT with one arm reaching, but cannot strike the withdrawing man's body. Preserve a broad black gap between their torsos and one clean hand-to-wrist contact, never fused anatomy. Draw ONE simple bold CURVED ROTATION ARROW just above and beside the retreating man's shoulder to indicate the quarter-turn, with a single arrowhead. Deliberate short backward/sideways steps, no running stride, fleeing turned back, successful hit, weapon, extra detached hand, prohibition symbol, circle badge, third figure or fine clothing detail.
Only TOP LEFT and TOP MIDDLE cells contain the TWO variations. CELLS 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 AND 9 MUST REMAIN COMPLETELY EMPTY PURE BLACK. No filler, labels or ornament.
